def _ccf_figure(ll) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_bar(x=ll.lags, y=ll.ccf, name="CCF")
    fig.add_vline(x=ll.peak_lag, line_dash="dash", line_color="crimson")
    fig.add_annotation(
        x=ll.peak_lag, y=ll.peak_corr,
        text=f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}", showarrow=True, arrowhead=2,
    )
    fig.update_layout(
        title=f"Cross-correlation  ρ(k)=corr({ll.x_name}ₜ, {ll.y_name}ₜ₊ₖ)   (k>0 ⇒ {ll.x_name} leads)",
        xaxis_title="lag k (days)", yaxis_title="correlation", height=340,
        margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=50, b=10),
    )
    return fig


def _line(series: pd.Series, title: str, yaxis: str) -> go.Figure:
    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=series.index, y=series.to_numpy(), mode="lines")
    fig.update_layout(title=title, yaxis_title=yaxis, height=300, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=40, b=10))
    return fig


def _render_results(result) -> None:
    ll = result.leadlag
    st.subheader("Results")

    c1, c2, c3 = st.columns(3)
    leader = "CL (futures)" if ll.x_leads else ("XLE" if ll.peak_lag < 0 else "contemporaneous")
    c1.metric("Lead-lag leader", leader, f"peak lag {ll.peak_lag}")
    if result.granger:
        g = result.granger["x->y"]
        c2.metric(f"Granger {SYMBOLS[LEAD]}→{SYMBOLS[LAG]}", f"p={g.p_value:.3f}",
                  "significant" if g.significant else "n.s.")
    if result.spot_check:
        c3.metric("CL=F vs FRED spot", f"{result.spot_check['median_abs_pct']:.1f}%",
                  f"{result.spot_check['common_days']} common days")

    st.plotly_chart(_ccf_figure(ll), use_container_width=True)

    gc, cc = st.columns(2)
    with gc:
        st.markdown("**Granger causality (both directions)**")
        if result.granger:
            rows = [
                {"direction": g.direction, "best lag": g.best_lag,
                 "p-value": round(g.p_value, 4), "significant": g.significant}
                for g in result.granger.values()

    if result.rolling_corr is not None and not result.rolling_corr.empty:

            use_container_width=True,

        rb.plotly_chart(
            _line(result.rolling_beta, f"Rolling β of {SYMBOLS[LAG]} to oil", "beta"),
            use_container_width=True,

def _demo_volume_data(start: str, end: str) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Synthetic storage + production data for demo when no EIA key is set."""
    import numpy as np

    dates_w = pd.date_range(start, end, freq="W-FRI")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(42)
    storage = 35_000 + rng.normal(0, 2000, len(dates_w)).cumsum().clip(-5000, 35000)
    storage_df = pd.DataFrame({"value": storage}, index=dates_w)
    storage_df.index.name = "date"

    dates_m = pd.date_range(start, end, freq="MS")

    prod_df = pd.DataFrame({"value": prod}, index=dates_m)

"""Diagnostic plots for microstructure signals.

Consumed by the dashboard's microstructure panel (``app/dashboard.py``).
Follows the dashboard's existing plotly conventions (see ``_ccf_figure`` /
``_line`` there): one figure per function, ~300px tall, tight margins.

The full AAPL golden day has ~1.5M events — far beyond what plotly renders
responsively — so figures decimate to :data:`MAX_PLOT_POINTS` evenly spaced
rows first. Uniform decimation preserves the session-scale shape (trend,
regime shifts) that these diagnostics exist to show; it deliberately drops
single-event spikes, which belong in an event-level view, not here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go

from oil_alpha.microstructure.kyles_lambda import KylesLambdaResult

#: Ceiling on rendered points per trace; ~5k keeps plotly interactive.
MAX_PLOT_POINTS: int = 5_000


def _decimate(df: pd.DataFrame, max_points: int = MAX_PLOT_POINTS) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Every k-th row so at most ``max_points`` rows survive (order kept)."""
    if len(df) <= max_points:
        return df
    step = math.ceil(len(df) / max_points)
    return df.iloc[::step]


def _clock(ns: pd.Series | pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """ITCH ns-since-midnight -> wall-clock timestamps (ET) for plot axes."""
    return pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(ns, dtype="int64"), unit="ns")


def ofi_vs_price_figure(events: pd.DataFrame) -> go.Figure:
    """Cumulative OFI vs microprice over the session, twin y-axes.

    Cumulative OFI (net signed order flow, shares) on the left axis and the
    microprice (dollars) on the right — visually co-moving lines are the
    qualitative signature of price impact that Kyle's lambda quantifies.
    """
    df = events[["timestamp_ns", "ofi", "microprice"]].copy()
    df["cum_ofi"] = df["ofi"].cumsum()
    df = _decimate(df)
    t = _clock(df["timestamp_ns"])

    fig = go.Figure()
    fig.add_scatter(x=t, y=df["cum_ofi"], mode="lines", name="cumulative OFI (sh)")
    fig.add_scatter(x=t, y=df["microprice"], mode="lines", name="microprice ($)",
                    yaxis="y2", line=dict(color="crimson"))
    fig.update_layout(
        title="Cumulative order-flow imbalance vs microprice",
        yaxis=dict(title="cumulative OFI (shares)"),
        yaxis2=dict(title="microprice ($)", overlaying="y", side="right"),
        legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02),
        height=340, margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=70, b=10),
    )
    return fig


def lambda_stability_figure(result: KylesLambdaResult) -> go.Figure:
    """Per-window Kyle's lambda across the session with the session aggregate.

    Trustworthy windows (``ok=True``) are solid bars; low-observation windows
    are greyed out so an illiquid stretch reads as "no evidence", not "zero
    impact". The dashed line is the whole-session estimate.

"""Load the C++ microstructure event stream as a pandas DataFrame (scaffold).

Follows the ``oil_volume.py`` wrapper pattern: importing this module never
fails, ``USING_CPP`` reports whether the ``signals_cpp`` extension is built.
Unlike ``oil_volume`` there is deliberately no pure-Python fallback — parsing
a 45 MB binary ITCH day in Python is exactly the workload the C++ layer
exists for, so a missing extension raises with a build hint instead.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import warnings

import pandas as pd

try:
    import signals_cpp as _cpp

    USING_CPP = True
except ImportError:
    _cpp = None  # type: ignore[assignment]
    USING_CPP = False

#: Columns of the event-stream DataFrame, in order.
EVENT_COLUMNS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "timestamp_ns", "ofi", "microprice", "best_bid", "best_ask",
    "bid_size", "ask_size",
)

# AAPL traded roughly $289-$293 on the golden day (2019-12-30, pre-split).
# Fixed-point (x10000) book bounds with headroom for the full session:
AAPL_GOLDEN_MIN_RAW: int = 2_800_000   # $280.00
AAPL_GOLDEN_MAX_RAW: int = 3_000_000   # $300.00


def load_micro_events(
    path: str,
    min_price_raw: int,
    max_price_raw: int,
    tick_size: int = 1,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Parse a symbol-filtered framed ITCH file into a per-update event frame.

    Returns a DataFrame with :data:`EVENT_COLUMNS`; ``attrs`` carries the
    ``skipped_one_sided`` and ``book_error_count`` diagnostics. Prices are
    ITCH fixed-point (dollars x 10000) on input, dollars in the output frame.

    A file with no book activity for the symbol (halted / illiquid session)
    returns an EMPTY frame with the right columns and emits a warning — it
    never raises. IO problems (missing/unreadable file) raise RuntimeError
    from the extension.
    """
    if not USING_CPP:
        raise ImportError(
            "signals_cpp extension not built — run `pip install -e .` "
            "(see cpp/signals_py/)"
        )
    raw = _cpp.events_from_file(path, min_price_raw, max_price_raw, tick_size)
    df = pd.DataFrame({c: raw[c] for c in EVENT_COLUMNS})
    df.attrs["skipped_one_sided"] = raw["skipped_one_sided"]
    df.attrs["book_error_count"] = raw["book_error_count"]
    if df.empty:
        warnings.warn(
            f"no microstructure events in {path!r} (halted/illiquid symbol, or "
            f"price bounds [{min_price_raw}, {max_price_raw}] never held a "
            "two-sided book)",
            stacklevel=2,
        )
    return df
